title: fr.linagora.twalk.consent.state.changed.v1
description: The user modified the data-processing consent state of a contact, a network or a persona. Produced by the Companion Gateway, the single writer of consent state (see ADR 0006). This is an operational event: the network and consent extensions are declared but optional (ADR 0007), because a consent change can span several networks and is itself about consent; network is set only for a single-network change, and consent is never set at all.

specversion.description: CloudEvents specification version. Fixed to 1.0 for all Twalk v1 events.

id.description: Deterministic identifier: the lowercase-hex sha256 of the UTF-8 string data.subject.type + ':' + data.subject.id + ':' + data.new_state + ':' + <networks> + ':' + data.occurred_at, where the parts are joined by single ASCII colons, each is the corresponding value verbatim (occurred_at exactly as serialized in this event, not reformatted), and <networks> is data.scope.networks sorted in ascending order and joined by single ASCII commas with no spaces, so a single network renders as just that value, with no comma. A third-party producer reproducing this string byte for byte gets the same id, so re-emitting the same recorded change is idempotent on the bus. The scope is part of the key on purpose: two decisions on the same subject, to the same state, at the same instant but over different networks are different decisions, and a key without the scope would collide them onto one id, which the bus would then deduplicate down to one.

source.description: URI of the consent resource on the Companion Gateway. Format: gateway://<domain>/consent.

type.description: CloudEvents type. Reverse-DNS convention with an explicit version suffix. Any breaking change to this schema requires incrementing the suffix (v2, v3, ...) rather than mutating v1.

time.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the Companion Gateway produced the event.

subject.description: Optional identifier of the affected subject (a contact's Matrix user ID, a persona id, or a network value). Mirrors data.subject.id for filtering convenience.

datacontenttype.description: Fixed to application/json for all Twalk v1 events.

dataschema.description: Optional URI pointing back to this JSON Schema. Recommended for third-party consumers that validate events dynamically.

traceparent.description: Optional W3C Trace Context traceparent header.

network.description: Twalk extension. Optional on this operational event: the Companion Gateway sets it only when data.scope.networks names exactly one network, and leaves it out otherwise. The authoritative scope is always data.scope.networks; this attribute exists so a single-network change can be filtered server-side on NATS.

consent.description: Twalk extension. Declared for envelope uniformity with the message-flow events, but never set on this event: there it labels the consent state of the event's subject, which on an event that announces a consent change is redundant with data.new_state at best and self-contradictory on a revocation, where the subject is already revoked while the event is the very decision that revoked it. Consumers read data.new_state. The Companion Gateway, the only producer, leaves this attribute out; an event that still carries it stays valid, and data.new_state wins.

type.description: What the consent decision applies to: a contact, a whole network, or a persona. A network subject carries that network's default consent state: it applies to every contact on that network for which no contact-scoped decision exists, and a contact-scoped decision for the same network always overrides it.

id.description: Identifier of the subject: a Matrix user ID for a contact, a persona id for a persona, and for a network subject the network value itself, in which case scope.networks holds exactly that one network.

subject.description: Who or what the consent decision applies to.

old_state.description: Consent state before the change. 'unset' means no decision had ever been recorded for this subject.

networks.description: Networks the decision applies to. A contact reachable on several networks gets one decision per scope.

scope.description: The perimeter of the consent decision.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the user took the decision. Part of the id natural key.

actor.description: Optional Matrix user ID of the human who took the decision.

reason.description: Optional free-text reason recorded with the decision, for the audit trail.
